header.title: Open 3D Viewer Studio
header.heroAlt: Open 3D Viewer Studio with a SketchUp model of a house on its plot; models and layers on the left, file properties on the right
header.label: 3D viewer
header.tagline: Open any building model you receive, without the program that made it
header.desc: Drop a SketchUp, Tekla, DWG or glTF file in your browser, or open IFC and Revit in the desktop app. Walk around the model, measure, cut it open and save it as IFC.

meta.description: Free, open-source 3D viewer for building models: IFC, Revit, SketchUp, Tekla, DWG/DXF, CityJSON, LandXML, glTF, OBJ, STL and PLY. Measure, section and save as IFC, in the browser and on Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.title: Open 3D Viewer Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

measure.alt: Two distance measurements on the garage of a house model, with the values and units in the panel on the right
measure.title: Measure right in the model
measure.desc: Click two points, edges or faces and read the distance, with the difference in X, Y and Z. Angles, areas, volumes and polygons too. Measurements stay in view until you clear them.

section.alt: House model with a section box at the first floor, showing the rooms and the furniture
section.title: Look inside with a section
section.desc: A section box or section plane cuts the model open, with filled cut faces. Slide each axis until you look at exactly the floor you need.

explode.alt: Bathroom model pulled apart per element, with the X, Y and Z sliders in the panel on the right
explode.title: See how it fits together
explode.desc: Pull the model apart, per storey or per element, by a percentage per axis. One view shows how a bathroom or a building is put together.

themes.alt: Top view of the house on its plot with an orthographic camera, in the dark theme
themes.title: Work the way you like
themes.desc: Pick one of five themes, from light and dark to Blueprint and high contrast. Top, front and side views and an orthographic camera are one key away, and every command can get the shortcut you want.

features.label: Features
features.heading: View, measure and section in one window
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

orbit.title: Orbit, pan and zoom
orbit.desc: Left drag orbits, middle drag pans, the wheel zooms to the cursor. F fits the whole model in view.

views.title: View cube and standard views
views.desc: Turn the model to a side with the view cube. Iso, top, front and right on 0 to 3, perspective or orthographic on P and O.

render.title: Solid, wireframe or with edges
render.desc: Switch between the render modes with S, W and E, and toggle the grid with G.

layers.title: Layers on and off
layers.desc: The explorer lists the layers with colour and count: IFC layers, Revit categories, SketchUp tags, Tekla classes or CAD layers. Turn them on or off one by one.

select.title: Properties of an element
select.desc: Click an element and read its properties. For the file you see the format, size, triangle count and dimensions.

flip.title: Other up axis
flip.desc: Is a model lying on its side because the file uses another up axis? One click stands it upright.

distance.title: Distances and angles
distance.desc: Measure between points, edges and faces, or between two elements. Every distance shows the difference in X, Y and Z.

area.title: Area, volume and polygon
area.desc: Measure an area or volume, or click a polygon. Choose the unit (mm, cm or m) and the number of decimals.

section.title: Section box and section plane
section.desc: Cut the model open with a box or a plane, with filled cut faces. The box can fit the selection.

explode.title: Exploded view
explode.desc: Pull the model apart per storey or per element, by a percentage per axis.

ifcrevit.title: Open IFC and Revit
ifcrevit.desc: The desktop app opens IFC and Revit (.rvt, .rfa), with levels, grids, rooms and saved views. IFC spaces start hidden in a layer of their own.

schedules.title: Revit schedules as a table
schedules.desc: A schedule from a Revit file opens as a table under the 3D view. Click a row and its elements are selected.

cad.title: SketchUp, Tekla and DWG/DXF
cad.desc: SketchUp from version 3, Tekla Structures (beta) and the faces of DWG and DXF drawings, in the browser and on the desktop.

geo.title: CityJSON and LandXML
geo.desc: Buildings from a CityJSON city model, at the highest level of detail per object, and terrain surfaces (TIN) from LandXML.

mesh.title: glTF, OBJ, STL and PLY
mesh.desc: The common 3D formats from design, scanning and printing software open too.

multi.title: Several models at once
multi.desc: Open replaces the model, Add puts another file next to it. Each model has its own eye to show or hide it.

saveifc.title: Save as IFC
saveifc.desc: Save any model the viewer opens as IFC 4, with storeys, classes, properties and materials. In the browser the file goes to your downloads.

themes.title: Five themes
themes.desc: Light, dark, Blueprint and two high-contrast variants, in the same window as the other OpenAEC apps.

shortcuts.title: Your own shortcuts
shortcuts.desc: Every command is in one list, shared by the ribbon, the title bar and the keyboard. Give any command your own key in the settings.

lang.title: Dutch and English
lang.desc: Choose the language of the window in the settings.

mcp.title: Let an AI assistant drive it
mcp.desc: Through the MCP server an AI assistant opens files, turns the camera, finds elements by property, measures and sections, in the window you see.

private.title: Your model stays with you
private.desc: Even in the browser nothing is uploaded: the file is read on your own computer.

update.title: Signed downloads and updates
update.desc: Every installer is signed. When the OpenAEC Installer has a newer version, the title bar says so and Update installs it.

download.title: Download v2026.44.18
download.lead: Free, no account needed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? The app also runs in the browser.
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open 3D Viewer Studio is made for a large screen. Open it on your computer, or try it here in the browser.

revit.title: Revit and IFC on the desktop
revit.desc: Revit files with levels, rooms, views and schedules as tables; IFC with storeys and layers.

formats.title: CityJSON, LandXML and DWG/DXF
formats.desc: New: city models, terrain surfaces and the faces of CAD drawings.

multi.title: Several models
multi.desc: Add puts a second file next to the first; each model gets its own eye.

shell.title: The OpenAEC window
shell.desc: Compact ribbon, explorer and properties, five themes and your own shortcuts, as in the other OpenAEC apps.

mcp.title: Exploded view for AI
mcp.desc: An AI assistant can now also pull the model apart through the MCP server.

signed.title: Signed for every platform
signed.desc: Windows with signed installer and uninstaller, macOS notarized by Apple, Linux with the OpenAEC key.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.44
whatsnew.title: Revit, IFC and new formats
whatsnew.desc: The renewed viewer: one app for desktop and browser, in the window of all OpenAEC apps, with more formats and signed downloads for every platform.

files.a: IFC and Revit (.rvt, .rfa) in the desktop app. SketchUp (version 3 and later), Tekla Structures (.db1, beta), DWG/DXF, CityJSON, LandXML, glTF, OBJ, STL and PLY in the desktop app and in the browser. Point clouds (E57, LAS), FBX, STEP and IGES do not open yet.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The browser version works in a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari with WebGPU. For IFC and Revit, and to connect an AI assistant, install the desktop app, most easily with the OpenAEC Installer.

price.a: Nothing. The viewer is free, with no account and no licence fees. The source code is LGPL-3.0; for Revit the desktop app uses an OpenAEC library with a licence of its own.

save.q: In which file format is my work saved?
save.a: The viewer does not change your file. Save as stores the model as IFC 4, with storeys, classes, properties and materials. Elements are written as triangles, not as parametric geometry.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows 10 and 11 (x64), macOS 11 or later (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (.deb, .rpm, AppImage), and in any browser with WebGPU.

practice.a: Yes. You open what you are sent from Revit, SketchUp, Tekla and CAD, and turn it into IFC 4 for an openBIM workflow. The IFC export is checked with IfcOpenShell. Classes come from the Revit category or the Tekla part; elements of an opened IFC file do not keep their class yet.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: With the MCP server that comes with the desktop app, Claude or another MCP client drives the viewer as you do: open files, take screenshots, choose views and layers, find and select elements, measure, section, explode and read Revit schedules. It stays on your own computer.

browser.q: Why does IFC not open in the browser?
browser.a: The IFC and Revit readers are not in the browser version yet. Use the desktop app for those. In the browser, .gltf files need their buffers embedded, and OBJ materials are not read yet.

privacy.a: No. Even in the browser the file is read on your own computer; nothing goes to a server.

notyet.q: What does it not do yet?
notyet.a: There is no undo, walk mode or hidden-line view yet. Textures become their average colour. The browser version freezes briefly while loading a large model and does not remember your settings yet.

rust.desc: One code base for the desktop app, the browser version and the MCP server.

iced.desc: The interface, native and as WebAssembly, without a web view or JavaScript framework.

wgpu.desc: An own 3D pipeline with 4x MSAA; the same code draws on the desktop and in the browser.

readers.desc: IFC through IFClite, DWG/DXF through acadrust, and OpenAEC's own readers for SketchUp, Tekla, PLY and Revit.

blueprint.desc: The window, design tokens, fonts and icons from the shared openaec-ui crate.

mcp.desc: open-3d-viewer-mcp drives the window on your screen over 127.0.0.1 with a random token.
